title: Book One: Resistance - Defining the Enemy
coreMove: Name the reasonable-sounding delay that appears at the threshold of meaningful work as Resistance before trusting it as caution.
sourcePressure: The source sidecar supports a stern framing of avoidance around meaningful work: Resistance is invisible, recurring, strongest around real work, and able to bury a calling if the reader keeps treating delay as innocent.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The weak version is generic procrastination advice, as if the problem were laziness instead of intelligent avoidance around work that would expose the self.

sourceAnchors.name: Hitler
sourceAnchors.detail: The sidecar says Hitler wanted to be an artist, moved to Vienna, applied to the Academy of Fine Arts and later the School of Architecture, and Resistance beat him.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The Vienna story should land as a severe warning about evasion hardening over time, not as a total explanation of history.

sourceAnchors.name: Vienna
sourceAnchors.detail: The sidecar identifies Vienna as the city Hitler moved to while pursuing art school admission.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: A young man can cross a continent toward art and still refuse the work that would make the calling real.

sourceAnchors.name: Academy of Fine Arts application
sourceAnchors.detail: The sidecar says Hitler applied to the Academy of Fine Arts before later applying to the School of Architecture.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: An application can look like commitment while the deeper pattern of refusal is already forming.

hook: Resistance is the enemy inside you
counterintuition: The problem is not laziness, it is fear
Your excuses are smarter than you think
tryThisNow: Set a timer and write for five minutes
Name one project you are avoiding
examples: a writer staring at a blank page
folder-cleaning as the only avoidance image

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person 'You' direct address, retrospective 'It took her three weeks to see', question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.domain: a nonprofit founder avoiding the first grant narrative by polishing the budget appendix
exampleSpecs.audience: founders and operators whose mission language hides the exposed ask they have not written
exampleSpecs.stakes: a neighborhood legal clinic loses a matching grant if the narrative is not submitted by Friday
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Grace closes the appendix spreadsheet, puts the untouched narrative field full-screen, and types the first ugly sentence before changing another line item.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: an unopened grant narrative with a polished appendix beside it
mustAvoid: checking email as the main delay

exampleSpecs.domain: an indie game designer delaying a playable demo through endless concept art
exampleSpecs.audience: creative technologists who keep improving the world around the thing that must be tested
exampleSpecs.stakes: a small festival submission requires a playable build, not more visual polish
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Etienne drags the sketch folder into an archive, connects the controller, and records one clumsy playable loop before drawing another creature.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a game controller beside twenty-seven creature sketches

exampleSpecs.domain: a choir soloist rehearsing fragments instead of recording the audition file
exampleSpecs.audience: performers who keep protecting the ideal version by refusing a recorded artifact
exampleSpecs.stakes: the audition portal closes at midnight and only one take has to be uploaded
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Rachel says 'one more run-through,' hears the phrase as Resistance, presses record, and uploads the imperfect take while her throat is still warm.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a phone voice-memo screen waiting on a red record button
mustAvoid: stage fright as the whole lesson

exampleSpecs.domain: a climate researcher revising figures instead of submitting the paper
exampleSpecs.audience: academic and technical workers whose standards can hide from verdict
exampleSpecs.stakes: a special issue closes and the model results will not matter if they stay private
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: It takes Luca three weeks to see that every figure revision happened after the submit button became available, so he writes the cover note and sends the manuscript.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a journal submission portal open behind a revised figure legend

exampleSpecs.domain: a hardware inventor cleaning the bench instead of filing the provisional patent
exampleSpecs.audience: builders who keep choosing tidy preparation over a commitment that creates public risk
exampleSpecs.stakes: a competitor demo is scheduled next month and the filing date matters
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Anya predicts the filing form will take all afternoon, starts it anyway, and discovers the real obstacle was pressing submit under her own name.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a patent form under a tray of sorted machine screws

exampleSpecs.domain: a new therapist postponing the first paid intake workshop
exampleSpecs.audience: new professionals whose care for quality hides fear of being chosen or rejected
exampleSpecs.stakes: a rented studio and twelve registrants will become a loss if the workshop is canceled again
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You watch James stop rewriting the handout, unlock the studio door, and greet the first registrant instead of sending another postponement note.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: twelve empty workshop chairs on a rented studio floor

skillTargets: distinguish real preparation from threshold displacement
identify when fear is evidence of meaningful exposure rather than a stop sign
separate a legitimate obstacle from Resistance borrowing responsible language
evaluate whether naming Resistance helps or overreaches in a blocked scenario

tryThisNowSpec: Open the project you have been circling and mark the one action that would make it visible to someone else; do that action before improving any support material.

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a direct second-person passage that asks the reader to inspect the timing of the excuse
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'
